title: Investigate ghost slab residency with cudaMallocAsync during KV prefetching
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Production clusters running steady continuous-batching workloads plus aggressive KV cache prefetching show slowly increasing GPU resident memory that is not reclaimed even after traffic drops. Behavior correlates with cudaMallocAsync buffers becoming 'resident' in pool arenas that are not being recycled; we observe long-lived 'ghost' slabs referenced by the allocator but apparently unreachable by any active KV cache object. This ticket tracks investigation, repro, short-term mitigations, and a fix path for allocator/stream synchronization and pool purge behavior.

Symptoms and scope:
- Memory metric: device resident shows +8–20% drift over 24–48h on some nodes under continuous batching workloads.
- Leak pattern: fragmentation + many small unreturned slabs (~16KB-512KB) accumulating in pool manager.
- Trigger conditions: observed with cudaMallocAsync enabled, KV cache prefetch enabled, and mixed synchronous/asynchronous request paths (inference + background prefetch threads).
- Impact: occasional OOM under high sustained load; increased tail latency due to additional GC activity on the host.

Reproduction steps (minimal):
1) Run runtime with CUDA driver 12.x and cudamallocasync enabled.
2) Enable KV prefetch with background workers prefetching 3x typical sequence length.
3) Use continuous batching traffic generator at 1000 qps with mixed sync/async routes.
4) Monitor device resident via nvidia-smi and runtime allocator metrics (pool_count, arena_resident_bytes, deferred_free_queue_len).
Expected: pool resident stabilizes. Observed: steady net increase in arena_resident_bytes.

Investigation notes and findings: 
- Heap snapshots (alloc-trace) from 2026-02-12 show deferred free queues growing; many entries point to frees enqueued on non-owner streams.
- cudaMallocAsync defers actual device memory free until the allocator's stream finishes work; if events/waits are used incorrectly (e.g., host threads calling cudaEventRecord on different streams), frees may be delayed indefinitely.
- The pool uses slab arenas keyed by block size, but we observed pointer churn where a freed device pointer becomes a new allocation in a different arena due to size rounding, leaving small residue slabs in original arena marked resident.
- A race between KV prefetch cancellation path and background evictor can leave host data structures dropped while device slab remains referenced by the allocator's internal lists (missing list unlink under concurrent freeing).
- Preliminary perf traces show cudaStreamWaitEvent + immediate host-side work that records events back-to-back; driver may keep resources resident longer.

Hypotheses: 
1) Improper stream affinity for deferred free operations causes frees to be queued on streams that never reach completion in some cancellation/error paths.
2) The slab pool's unlink logic is not fully atomic for the mixed-size reallocation scenario, leading to orphaned slab metadata.
3) Background prefetch pattern (bulk alloc + staggered KV insert) amplifies fragmentation and prevents coalescing heuristics from kicking in.

Short-term mitigations proposed (canary rollout):
- Force a periodic pool purge in the allocator (configurable interval) to forcibly release arenas older than X seconds.
- Reduce aggressive KV prefetch batch size to limit temporal concurrency.
- Add a runtime flag to disable cudaMallocAsync for a small percentage of nodes to measure impact.
- Add telemetry counters and an alert when deferred_free_queue_len grows past threshold.

Long-term fixes: 
- Ensure correct stream affinity: ensure frees are enqueued on the same stream the memory was allocated or add robust event-based draining.
- Harden slab unlinking with atomic CAS or global mutex path for corner-case reallocation sizes.
- Add allocator unit tests that simulate prefetch cancellation + concurrent evictor to catch leaks in CI.
- Evaluate using cuMemPoolTrim or explicit cuMemRelease on trusted intervals if supported by drivers.

Artifacts and references: 
- Reproducer harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/tree/main/repro/kv-prefetch-leak (attached).
- Heapshots & perf traces: https://confluence.redwood/KB/kv-prefetch-heapshots (internal).
- Draft PR w/ purge timer & telemetry: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1342
- Related tickets: ENG-24109 (allocator telemetry), ENG-23678 (KV prefetch backoff tuning).

Acceptance criteria / done when: 
- Root cause identified and documented with a minimal repro.
- Short-term mitigations rolled to canary and show no increasing resident trend over 72h.
- Fix PR for stream-affine frees or slab unlinking merged and validated on staging.
- New unit tests added to prevent regression and telemetry in prod to detect recurrence.
